correctness.rationale: For positive n and odd prime p, the binomial identity gives p E_p(n)=C-A with C=binom(n-1,2p-1) and A=(p+1)(n_1-1) times the indicator of p dividing n. Lucas modulo p gives zero if p does not divide n and n_1-1 modulo p otherwise, so p divides C-A. Since A is even and p odd, Lucas modulo 2 then gives the mask condition, also for n<2p. For the printed floor sum, fix digit e_h of j and let f_h be the h-th zero position of m-1, indexed from zero. Exactly the first r=f_h-h one positions of m contribute, with coefficient 2^(h+1) plus the terms 2^(h+a-1) for 2<=a<=r, which sums to 2^f_h even when r=1. Thus j fills exactly the complementary bits of m-1 without carries, yielding a bijection onto all 2^z mask classes, including the residue n=0 modulo 2^L via n-1. Dividing the defining equality by two gives the stated fractional part. The proof is universal; the independent limited check through p=47 and the larger author-recorded checks in VERIFICATION.md/verify.py are corroboration only; the uploaded script was inspected, not executed.
